key_insight: HypoExplore reframes neural architecture search as a hypothesis-driven scientific inquiry: an agentic loop uses an LLM to propose and refine architecture hypotheses, then implements and evaluates them via evolutionary branching to discover better models for visual recognition.
problem_solved: Addresses the slow, manual, and often unguided process of designing neural architectures for vision by automating ideation, implementation, and evaluation while balancing reuse of validated design principles and the exploration of novel ideas.
method: Agentic experiment loop: ideate (LLM-generated hypotheses) → implement (instantiate architectures) → evaluate (train/measure on vision tasks) → improve (select and refine).
Evolutionary branching: build new hypotheses by choosing parent hypotheses and creating variants to explore architecture design spaces.
Active hypothesis exploration: dual strategy balancing exploitation of validated principles and exploration of novel hypotheses to maximize discovery efficiency.
impact: Enables faster, more systematic discovery of competitive vision architectures and reduces human trial-and-error, helping researchers and engineers scale creative design and evaluation of models.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the agentic loop (Ideate → Implement → Evaluate → Improve) with an LLM icon at the ideation step.
Evolutionary tree diagram showing branching hypotheses and selection of promising branches.
Bar/line chart comparing discovery speed or performance of HypoExplore vs. baseline NAS/manual design (conceptual).
Icon collage: LLM + neural network + dataset/metrics to convey automated hypothesis-driven architecture search.
paper_title: Agentic Discovery with Active Hypothesis Exploration for Visual Recognition
paper_authors: Jaywon Koo, Jefferson Hernandez, Ruozhen He, Hanjie Chen, Chen Wei
